title: Drug resistance and molecular epidemiology of pediatric
abstract: To investigate antimicrobial susceptibility and molecular typing of recent pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae strains, analyze the correlations between drug resistance, pneumonia severity, and strain types, and provide evidence for precise M. pneumoniae infection management. Standard M. pneumoniae isolation and culture were applied to bronchoalveolar lavage fluid from 325 M. pneumoniae-infected children, with 23S rRNA resistance mutation detection. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing (eight antibiotics, microbroth dilution) was performed on 154 culture-positive strains, alongside multiple locus variable-number tandem repeat analysis (MLVA), whole-genome sequencing, and single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) genotyping. M. pneumoniae showed high macrolide resistance (99.35% for erythromycin and azithromycin), but high susceptibility to moxifloxacin/levofloxacin, with minocycline/doxycycline sensitivity at 98.71%. The 23S rRNA mutations occurred in 97.4% (150/154). MLVA type 4-5-7-2 dominated (135/154), with minor types totaling 15 cases. SNP typing clustered strains into four groups, mostly EC1 (138/154), with four genes showing cross-cluster mutations. Southern Chinese M. pneumoniae strains exhibit high macrolide resistance but good minocycline/doxycycline susceptibility, with EC1-cluster dominance driving rapid spread. This supports individualized therapy and epidemic trend tracking for pediatric M. pneumoniae lung infections. This study sheds light on why many children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia do not respond well to common macrolide antibiotics-over 99% of strains in Southern China are resistant. It identifies effective alternative drugs and pinpoints the dominant spreading strain, helping doctors choose precise treatments. For public health, it provides key data to track outbreaks, guiding targeted surveillance and better management of pediatric respiratory infections post-COVID-19.

title: Microscopic and molecular Cryptosporidium parvum infection in individuals with gastrointestinal symptoms in South Khorasan, Iran.
abstract: Cryptosporidium spp., an opportunistic protozoan affecting humans and animals, ranks as the third leading global cause of diarrheal disease. This study aimed to molecularly identify C. parvum in patients with gastrointestinal symptom in Birjand, South Khorasan province, Iran. Cryptosporidium parvum was molecularly confirmed and characterized using nested PCR and sequencing of the 18S rRNA gene on 160 stool samples from symptomatic patients in Birjand. Phylogenetic analysis was conducted to assess genetic relationships. The resulting phylogenetic trees and haplotype networks were compared. In this study, molecular prevalence was 8.75 (14/160). Sequencing confirmed all positives as C. parvum. Phylogenetic clustering revealed overlap between human isolates and animal-derived strains. Molecular epidemiology is critical for mapping Cryptosporidium transmission. Phylogenetic evidence supports zoonotic cycles in South Khorasan, informing targeted public health strategies.

title: VENAS2: Bidirectional Mutation Modeling for Genomic Surveillance Reveals Reversions and Hidden Transmission Links in Pathogens.
abstract: Accurately resolving pathogen evolution is essential for genomic surveillance, yet existing approaches often assume unidirectional mutation accumulation and fail to capture reversions that obscure lineage classification and transmission dynamics. Here we present VENAS2, a scalable framework that integrates genomic, temporal and geographic information to construct spatiotemporal evolutionary networks while explicitly modeling bidirectional mutational processes. Applied to 7.25 million SARS-CoV-2 genomes from GISAID between December 2019 and June 2024, VENAS2 reconstructed the evolutionary history of SARS-CoV-2 and precisely inferred the temporal dynamics of major variants of concern. Further application to the Viridian dataset revealed 4,654 distinct genomic sites with at least one potential reversion event, providing a systematic view of potential reversion signals during viral evolution. Extending to Mycobacterium tuberculosis, VENAS2 delineated major lineages and identified over threefold additional transmission clusters beyond conventional genomic distance-based methods, uncovering hidden links enriched for drug-resistant strains. These results demonstrate VENAS2's capacity to uncover cryptic evolutionary processes across viruses and bacteria, providing a generalizable platform that bridges genomic surveillance with actionable public health response.

title: Hereditary ATTR amyloidosis in Italy: pathogenic variant patterns and clinical profiles from a multicenter genetic dataset.
abstract: Hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRv) is a rare, progressive multisystem disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the TTR gene. This study aimed to describe the distribution of TTR pathogenic variants and associated clinical phenotypes across Italy using data from a large national genetic testing cohort. This retrospective study analyzed genetic and clinical data from individuals referred for TTR gene sequencing at a single reference laboratory between June 2016 and December 2023. Coding exons 2-4 and exon-intron boundaries of the TTR gene were sequenced by the Sanger method. Variants were classified according to ACMG/AMP criteria. Descriptive analyses summarized variant frequencies, regional distributions, and genotype-phenotype correlations. One hundred ninety-five individuals were included, comprising 94 affected patients and 101 asymptomatic carriers. Mean age was 56.8 years, 57.9% were male. Nineteen TTR pathogenic variants were identified, with five accounting for 86% of cases: Phe84Leu (34.4%), Val50Met (23.6%), Val142Ile (11.3%), Ile88Leu (10.3%), and Glu109Gln (6.7%). Phe84Leu predominated in Southern Italy, Val50Met was mainly observed in Lazio. Among affected individuals, 39.4% showed a mixed phenotype, 37.2% neurological, and 23.4% cardiac. Variant-specific patterns were confirmed: Phe84Leu was associated with neurological symptoms, Val142Ile and Ile88Leu with cardiac involvement, and Val50Met and Glu109Gln with multisystemic manifestations. Carpal tunnel syndrome (60.6%), cardiac pathology (66.0%), and sensory neuropathy (74.5%) were the most frequent findings. These findings expand current knowledge of ATTRv molecular epidemiology in a non-endemic setting and emphasize the need for standardized diagnostic pathways, regional genetic screening, and multidisciplinary management to improve early recognition and care.
journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology

title: Detection of the EAST AFRICA-2 topotype of serotype O foot-and-mouth disease virus in Ethiopia provides evidence of changing epidemiology in the Horn of Africa.
abstract: This study describes the first detection of the serotype O, EAST AFRICA-2 (O/EA-2) topotype of foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV) in Ethiopia. Samples were collected from FMD outbreaks affecting cattle and small ruminants during 2024-2025. Molecular analyses assigned 41/49 sequences to the O/EA-2 topotype which has not been previously detected in the country. These sequences shared close genetic identity (99.5%) to those from Sudan and Kenya, highlighting the transboundary expansion of this lineage into the Horn of Africa. Virus neutralization testing demonstrated antigenic match of two representative field isolates to five commercially available FMD vaccines. The emergence of O/EA-2 alters Ethiopia's viral landscape, which was previously dominated by the O/EA-3 and O/EA-4 topotypes. These findings motivate further studies to monitor the spread of this topotype and encourage authorities to adopt well-matched high-potency vaccines to mitigate the clinical impacts of outbreaks due to this lineage.
journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases

title: First epidemiological and molecular characterization of bovine leukemia virus in Holstein dairy cattle from two cities in Shandong Province, China.
abstract: Bovine leukemia virus (BLV) is the etiological origin of enzootic bovine leukosis, a chronic lymphoproliferative disorder causing significant economic losses to the global cattle industry. Shandong Province in eastern China is a major dairy cattle-breeding region. However, the molecular prevalence and genetic characteristics of BLV in this area remain unclear. In this study, 289 blood samples were collected from Holstein dairy cattle across three large-scale commercial farms in Shandong Province, China, and BLV infection was determined using nested PCR targeting the long terminal repeat (LTR) of the virus. Of 289 samples, 59 (20.4%) were positive for BLV provirus. Phylogenetic analysis was performed based on 423 bp partial sequences of the env-gp51 gene from 24 BLV isolates, which were positive for BLV provirus by PCR targeting both the LTR and the env-gp51 gene. Maximum likelihood phylogenetic trees revealed that the 24 BLV sequences from Shandong Province were clustered into three distinct genotypes-namely, Genotypes-4, -6, and -7-among the 12 known BLV genotypes worldwide. Bayesian phylogenetic trees indicated that BLV sequences belonging to Genotypes-4 and -6 were further classified into four and two distinct phylogenetic clusters, respectively. This study reports the coexistence of Genotype-4 (G4-1, G4-2, G4-3, and G4-4), Genotype-6 (G6-1 and G6-2), and Genotype-7 in the cattle population from two cities in Shandong Province. These findings provide important baseline information on the molecular epidemiology and genetic diversity of BLV in Shandong Province.

title: Fluctuations in Environmental Resource Availability Alter the Oscillatory Tragedy of the Commons
abstract: Environmental noise in real-world complex systems--including fluctuations in temperature, humidity, and related environmental conditions--inevitably modulates individual metabolic capacity and, consequently, the efficiency of public-resource utilization. Yet conventional evolutionary game models incorporating environmental feedback treat resource dynamics deterministically. Here, we incorporate stochastic fluctuations into a noise-corrected replicator-dynamics framework. Theoretical analysis and stochastic birth-death simulations yield a counterintuitive result: moderate environmental noise stabilizes, rather than destabilizes, the interior fixed point across diverse payoff landscapes, while suppressing or eliminating catastrophic oscillations. These findings reframe environmental variability not merely as a perturbation but as a mechanism that fosters strategy coexistence and sustainable resource use in complex social and ecological systems.
